name: Berlusconism
summary: Berlusconism is the leader-centred liberal-conservative politics of Silvio Berlusconi and Forza Italia: liberista economics and tax cutting, strong anti-communism, Atlanticism, a populist appeal of a businessman against the old political class and the judiciary, and a strong premiership. It is a pragmatic catch-all of the Italian centre right, Catholic-friendly but not confessional, with free votes on moral questions.
scope: Berlusconi's political project from the 1994 'discesa in campo' through his governments (1994, 2001-06, 2008-11) and Forza Italia/Popolo della Libertà, as described in the Wikipedia article on Berlusconism and the 1994 launch message. Excludes the Lega Nord and post-fascist allies' own programs, and Forza Italia's post-2013 forms. Many answers are low-confidence inferences because Berlusconism was a personalised, loosely programmatic movement.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Forza Italia backed a social market economy and Berlusconi said a democracy cannot leave citizens in poor conditions, so a public safety net is accepted; healthcare itself was not a signature issue.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The 1994 launch message called for a state "liberale in politica e liberista in economia" and accused the left of distrusting the free market, private enterprise and profit.

public-ownership.rationale: Berlusconi's liberista programme and his entrepreneur image point away from state ownership, but his governments kept state control of ENI, ENEL and Finmeccanica and blocked the foreign takeover of Alitalia in 2008.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: His signature 2001 Contract with the Italians promised two flat-ish income tax rates (33% and 23%), a pro-taxpayer rather than redistributive line.

property-fundamental.rationale: Defence of private enterprise and property against a feared communist heir left is the core of the 1994 message.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Liberismo and deregulation of the economy were central; adherents resist tighter corporate regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Liberal wing wanted a minimal state but the party also championed a social market economy and promised higher minimum pensions, so adherents are split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective ownership is the sort of left-wing economics the 1994 message attacks; adherents reject it.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Berlusconi named drugs among evils to fight in the 1994 message; his governments toughened drug law.

strong-leader.rationale: Berlusconism is described as a leader-centred movement with a light party, messianic self-image and push for a stronger premiership.

state-harmful.rationale: The party's ideal was a friendly minimal state serving citizens, but not abolition of the state; the state is still needed for order and justice.

decide-locally.rationale: Forza Italia's northern wing backed political and fiscal federalism, and Berlusconi pursued devolution to regions, though southern members were lukewarm.

traditional-family.rationale: A Catholic-but-not-confessional party, with family central to Italian centre-right rhetoric; later Berlusconi accepted civil unions, so not strongly.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Berlusconi only came to favour civil unions in 2013, implying marriage itself was not backed. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

abortion-legal.rationale: Moral questions were left to a free vote and the party followed the Church on the 2005 stem-cell referendum, so adherents are split.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Secular Creed called the party Catholic but not confessional and secular but not secularist; genuinely balanced.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The launch message is patriotic ("L'Italia è il paese che amo") and the coalition included Alleanza Nazionale; preservation of heritage is a mild centre-right theme.

gradual-change.rationale: Berlusconi promised a "liberal revolution" and big institutional reform yet is a conservative-liberal; split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: His government passed the 2002 Bossi-Fini law with expulsions of illegal immigrants and a 2008 Libya treaty to curb arrivals.

free-trade.rationale: Described as liberista and pro-free trade in economics.

nation-first.rationale: Strongly Atlanticist and EPP-member yet increasingly Eurosceptic, with a populist side; mixed.

open-borders.rationale: Bossi-Fini and anti-illegal-immigration measures reject open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Entrepreneurial optimism and pro-growth liberismo are central.

revolution-justified.rationale: A defender of order and the market who calls for liberal reform within democracy, and who presents the left as the radical menace.

central-planning.rationale: He attacks the left as heirs of communism and defends the free market.

socialized-markets.rationale: Private enterprise and profit, not public or worker ownership, are the stated ideal.

basic-income.rationale: Social-market welfare but work-and-enterprise emphasis; unconditional income not on the agenda.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Liberista and pro-free trade; protectionism clashes with that.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Free-market economics, with a state meant not to direct the economy.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Berlusconism is built on opposition to communism and defence of private enterprise and profit, so abolishing wage labour is the opposite of its program.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Liberismo in the Berlusconian sense means open markets, not abolition of monetary institutions; Forza Italia took part in euro-era institutions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Berlusconism is liberista and anti-statist; Italian fascist corporatism is not endorsed despite Mussolini remarks.

one-party-rule.rationale: Presents himself as defending freedom against illiberal left; competes within a multi-party democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Italy is a republic and Forza Italia is a republican party; there is no monarchist platform.

democracy-best.rationale: Berlusconism operates within electoral democracy and invokes freedom, though adherents attack judges and critics for limiting elected leaders.

direct-votes.rationale: Populist appeal but no platform for referenda; Berlusconi pushed constitutional reform confirmed by referendum, split.

workers-councils.rationale: Council communism is a left idea the movement opposes. The sources set out the underlying principle but do not state a position on this specific statement.

right-to-secede.rationale: Northern members backed federalism, not secession; Berlusconi remained a national-unity politician.

natural-rulers.rationale: Leader-cult and self-made-man elitism, but no explicit doctrine of natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Constitutionally democratic movement; rejects violence though no explicit statement. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

separate-church-state.rationale: The party called itself Catholic but not confessional and secular but not secularist.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Secular Creed rejects a confessional party; free votes on moral questions.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Liberista but still wants the state to enforce justice and order.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Berlusconism is civic-national and tolerated immigration quotas; not an ethnic-nation program.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Anti-communism and rejection of the left's class framing are central.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Liberista market stance and attack on the left favour opportunity, not outcome.

civilizational-union.rationale: Berlusconi called for Israel in the EU and Russia ties yet remained Western-oriented; unclear.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy was not part of Berlusconism, which stressed enterprise and growth; adherents plausibly accept the idea mildly but give it no weight, so left neutral.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Entrepreneurial optimism of Berlusconism contradicts it.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Optimistic about enterprise but not an accelerationist programme.

restore-past-order.rationale: Looks forward with entrepreneurial and liberal revolution talk, not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Berlusconi presented himself as a pragmatic doer and businessman; critics note populist pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: The movement sought power through elections and presented itself as the defender of freedom within democratic institutions, not through direct action.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Berlusconism meant entrepreneurial optimism and modernisation, so a return to hunter-gatherer life is flatly outside it.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Rejects communist distribution in favour of profit-driven markets. The sources set out the underlying principle but do not state a position on this specific statement.

production-for-use.rationale: The 1994 message defends profit and private enterprise against the left, which rejects production for use rather than profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The 1994 message defends profit and enterprise against the left.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Berlusconi cast the left as heirs of communism and his movement as the defence of liberty against it; proletarian dictatorship is the target of that rhetoric.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation belongs to the communist model the movement defined itself against; it favours private property and enterprise.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A liberista movement treats capitalism and free trade as sources of prosperity; the Leninist thesis is a left claim it opposes.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal in politics; libertarian-leaning social attitudes mixed with Catholic influence.

conscription.rationale: Italy abolished conscription in 2004 under his government; adherents accepted a professional army.

state-as-business.rationale: Berlusconi, a businessman, promised to run the country like a company; the movement is described as entrepreneurial.

media-academia-power.rationale: Berlusconi claimed hostile judiciary and press were left-wing; his own media empire contested it, mild agreement.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not part of Berlusconism; mainstream centre-right.

organic-representation.rationale: Liberal parliamentary democracy, not corporatist representation.

total-state.rationale: The movement presents itself as defender of freedom against illiberal state. The sources set out the underlying principle but do not state a position on this specific statement.

national-rebirth.rationale: The 1994 launch promised "un nuovo miracolo italiano" after the old political class failed, a rebirth theme.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not part of a liberal-conservative Atlanticist outlook.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Personalist loyalty to the leader existed but no doctrine of feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom-like duties contradict the liberal-in-politics, liberista-in-economics stance, though the topic is historical.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Described himself as pro-Israel and believed Israel should join the EU.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The sources record no position, and Berlusconi's own foreign focus was pro-Israel, but a right of return for diasporas was not a theme.

revive-national-language.rationale: Italian is not a revival case; adherents would be indifferent to language revival as a political goal.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic control of companies is a left program; Berlusconi's side backs owners and private enterprise instead.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He promised tax cuts and public spending while Italy had high debt; adherents split.

economic-freedom.rationale: The 1994 message ties political liberty and a liberal state with liberista economics.

rule-by-example.rationale: Leader-centred but not based on moral example.

force-without-un.rationale: Backed Letter of the Eight and the Iraq invasion without a UN mandate.

class-collaboration.rationale: Anti-class-struggle with entrepreneurs and workers as partners, a Berlusconian message.

dominated-front.rationale: Forza Italia joined the EPP and Berlusconi was strongly Atlanticist, so aligning against Western powers is foreign to it.

workers-nation.rationale: A national-line labour strategy is a left-wing organising idea; Berlusconism's anti-class-struggle outlook rejects it.

ban-interest.rationale: A liberista, business-owner movement defends credit and finance, so a ban on interest is plainly rejected.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Berlusconi, though praising Mussolini in part, criticised the Fascist racial laws, according to the Wikipedia article.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Marxist view of the state is the one the movement attacks as communist legacy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Mixed; stress on legal integration but no assimilationist programme in the sources.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy claim not part of mainstream Berlusconism.

proportional-representation.rationale: Berlusconi's governments changed electoral law several times for advantage; no fixed principle.

national-mission.rationale: Berlusconism has no doctrine of spreading Italy's government abroad; its foreign policy was alliance with the US, not mission.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Conservative/populist right rejects the structural claim.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The 1994 message blames the old political class for debt and illegal financing, though Berlusconi was himself accused of corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The movement's Catholic-leaning liberal conservatism stands against eugenic controls on reproduction.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Documented stance absent; a law-and-order movement is wary of prosecuting security forces but liberal democracy accepts accountability, so neutral.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Minimal-state ideal but social market elements.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: A liberal-conservative party that criticised racial laws does not advocate discouraging mixed marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Liberal democratic basis, though critics note remarks.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A doctrinal dispute inside Marxism; the movement rejects socialism wholesale.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The question concerns settler states like Israel, where Berlusconi was pro-Israel, yet he never discussed settler colonialism; neutral.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Italy has a uniform civil code and no one campaigns otherwise.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Catholic-oriented party supports religion class in schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Soviet-state doctrine; the movement is anti-communist at its root.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Elected mandate was central to his legitimacy claim.

population-transfer.rationale: Nothing in Berlusconism supports transferring minorities; it operated within liberal-democratic norms.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He backed wars with the US, but libertarian principle not a feature.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about competition between individuals or in markets, and this statement now asks only about struggle between peoples.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about competition between individuals or in markets, and this statement now asks only about struggle between peoples.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: His coalition included post-fascists, so not keen on bans, but anti-communist.

separated-powers.rationale: He attacked the judiciary as persecutor and wanted a stronger premier, yet backed separating magistrates' careers.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leninist party theory is the communism the movement was founded to oppose.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Social-market and Christian democrat wing want help, others market first.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not a theme of Berlusconism; a market-optimist and Catholic stance would blame institutions or policies, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Lega allies argued this while Forza Italia's liberal wing was more relaxed; adherents are split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The movement is built around elections and a leader chosen by voters; sortition is far from it.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price fixing contradicts liberismo, which distrusts state interference in markets.

party-controls-media.rationale: Liberal stance, though he himself held media dominance as owner.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of the army is a communist or fascist feature, foreign to a liberal-democratic movement.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Light party with little internal structure, but loyalty to leader.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Forza Italia joined the EPP and its Christian-democratic wing was pro-European, but after 2011 he grew Eurosceptic. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Pro-presidentialism for the premier; not head of state.

clerical-rule.rationale: Forza Italia called itself Catholic but not confessional and secular but not intolerant, rejecting rule by clerics.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A revolutionary-defeatist slogan belonging to Leninism; the movement is anti-communist and patriotic.

recall-officials.rationale: The sources give no position on recall; a populist but leader-centred movement has mixed incentives.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Berlusconi's governments were strongly Atlanticist and backed US wars, so ending alliances is rejected.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Banning rentals is a collectivist idea at odds with private property and enterprise.

people-in-arms.rationale: Replacing professional forces with an armed populace is not part of an Atlanticist, order-minded centre right.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The question concerns divided nations such as Korea or Ireland; Berlusconism has no relevant doctrine.

death-penalty.rationale: Not a Forza Italia plank; Catholic influence.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Moral questions were left to a free vote in Forza Italia, so adherents split between Catholic and liberal wings.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Italian law is by descent and coalition kept it.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's point about conformity is outside Berlusconism's recorded concerns; neutral.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A decolonisation claim; Atlanticist liberal movement would not endorse it.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Berlusconi pursued constitutional reform through parliament, put to referendum in 2006, not through an elected constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The launch message presented the movement as defending freedom against an illiberal state, so trading freedoms for growth contradicts it.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Italy relied on the NATO umbrella and Berlusconi was Atlanticist, so an independent deterrent was not pursued.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Berlusconi turned critical of European institutions and Merkel after 2011, but the liberal wing accepts independent central banks; split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Berlusconi was pro-Israel but the sources record no view on land-for-peace.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The movement treats private property and enterprise as fundamental, not as conditional on service to the common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate within the Marxist left; Berlusconism treated the USSR as communist and sources record no more.

collective-defense.rationale: Berlusconi's governments were strongly Atlanticist and supported US military ventures, which assumes NATO solidarity.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Warm to Putin; after Crimea visit; contested.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The party was Catholic-friendly, followed the Church on the 2005 stem-cell referendum, and would not curb church property or power.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The sources give no position; federalists in the party might welcome it while others would not.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Italy is a republic and Forza Italia a republican party; sacred rulers are not part of Berlusconism, even if critics noted his messianic self-image.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Two-rate plan of 33% and 23% and a flat-tax discourse.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He claimed persecution by judges but backed rule-of-law language; mixed.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not a Berlusconist theme; neutral.

leader-cult.rationale: Critics say he fostered a cult; adherents embraced his centrality.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Internal Marxist-Leninist doctrine; Berlusconism rejects socialism altogether.

land-redistribution.rationale: Seizing estates violates the movement's defence of private property.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentism is not part of Berlusconism, which stood for liberal-democratic Atlanticism.

common-currency.rationale: Italy entered euro; Berlusconi later critical of it.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic unions are not part of Berlusconism, which favoured the EU and NATO frameworks.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: A Bundist or minority-rights concept the sources do not tie to Berlusconism; neutral.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is the left worldview Berlusconi opposed as communism's legacy.

no-bailouts.rationale: Liberista principle says yes but the movement was populist and protective of firms and jobs; split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He attacked judges as obstructing elected will.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs contradict Berlusconi's liberismo and free-trade stance.

moral-incentives.rationale: The movement stands for profit and enterprise as motives, rejecting moral incentives replacing them.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Foquismo is a revolutionary-left idea; Berlusconism defended electoral democracy.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Berlusconism trusts markets and private enterprise to produce prosperity and sees no inevitable collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Berlusconi apologised to Libya and built ties there, but cultivating influence in former colonies was not a program; neutral.

delink-world-market.rationale: Breaking economic ties contradicts liberismo and free trade.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis alien to Berlusconism; adherents would say workers prosper in capitalism.

elective-rulers.rationale: The movement's legitimacy rested on the electoral mandate, though the question asks about versus inheritance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Berlusconi wanted a stronger premier and halving the Chamber, but accepted parliamentary government; split.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Berlusconi launched Forza Italia by announcing he would enter politics to defend freedom, the opposite of withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Berlusconi owned mass-market television and critics argued it pacified viewers; adherents deny this claim.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory contradicts the movement's free-trade liberismo.

party-own-road.rationale: A debate within communism with no relevance; the movement opposes communism outright.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Berlusconi praised Mussolini as a good leader in 2013 and resisted treating antifascism as the republic's founding value, though he criticised the racial laws.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The 1994 message accuses the left of being communism's heirs and asks for liberal freedom; Berlusconi framed communism as the main totalitarian threat while also criticising Nazi alliance.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American question with no recorded Berlusconist view; neutral.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Berlusconi admired Putin, yet a liberal West-oriented party insists on liberal democracy; split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Italy's republican tradition and Berlusconi's liberal stance reject an armed-forces political role.

office-by-exam.rationale: A populist, business-run movement favours elected or appointed leaders over exam-based mandarins.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Liberista openness conflicts with Italian patriotism in strategic firms; split.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The party left moral questions to free votes; liberal wing supports easy divorce, Italy having legalised divorce in the 1970s.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandates and instant recall contradict a leader-centred, party-light movement.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Liberista wing of Forza Italia favoured private provision of pensions, though no document opened states this precisely.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Communal ownership of land contradicts the defence of private property.

single-official-language.rationale: Italian is the common language, but Berlusconism has no program restricting minority languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Liberista openness to investment means no ban on foreign land purchases.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Berlusconi's television empire and entrepreneurial optimism celebrated consumption; critics said this fostered consumerism.

corporate-influence.rationale: Critics said his media and business interests gave him too much power, but adherents reject the claim of excessive corporate influence.

residents-only-property.rationale: Restricting property purchase conflicts with liberista property rights.

job-guarantee.rationale: The launch message pledged support to those creating jobs, i.e. the private sector, rather than the state as employer of last resort.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Adherents appeal to law and order, though Berlusconi himself attacked judges and ad personam laws; mild.

non-intervention.rationale: Berlusconi signed the letter of the eight and backed the Afghan and Iraq wars, rejecting absolute non-intervention.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A conspiracy against the nation by a minority is not a Berlusconian theme; his enemy was the left and the judges.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: A Catholic-influenced party that endorsed traditional family structure rejects abolishing legal marriage.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Atlanticist and EPP-member yet increasingly Eurosceptic; split on primacy of national law.

religious-nation.rationale: The party was a secular party in the sense of not defining the nation religiously.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary relations are an East Asian imperial idea unrelated to Berlusconism.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: A communist detail; adherents defend all private property and so neither rise nor fall on this distinction.

defeat-communism.rationale: Berlusconi's 1994 launch framed the left as communism's heirs and nostalgics and called for a bloc of freedom against them, and anti-communism is a named component of Berlusconism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: A social market economy approach with a liberista tilt favours mixed public and private delivery of services.

religion-illusion.rationale: Forza Italia called itself a Catholic party though not confessional, so it rejects the claim that religion is a mere illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The 1994 message defends the market and private enterprise as engines of well-being and jobs.

treaties-binding.rationale: An indigenous-treaty question without relevance to Italy; neutral.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Anarchist or communitarian reorganisation is far from a liberista, party-and-leader movement.

majority-settlement.rationale: A liberal-democratic movement would not promote majority settlement in minority regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Berlusconism defends capitalism and the market, so a third way is refused.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Berlusconi described himself as pro-Israel and condemned the racial laws, so Holocaust denial is out of bounds.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Berlusconi came to support civil unions in 2013 and Italy decriminalised same-sex relations long before; criminalising would be rejected.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The movement presented itself as defending freedom against an illiberal left, and competed in elections.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: A non-confessional, secular-in-politics party rejects state punishment of blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Berlusconi apologised to Libya for colonial crimes; exploitative rule is not endorsed.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The movement is pro-West and pro-Israel; an Islamic duty of jihad is outside it, so it rejects the premise.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Contradicts the party's non-confessional character and liberal-democratic framework.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Critical-theory framework rejected by a populist, anti-left movement.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Catholic-influenced centre right has been cool; Berlusconi's era predates the debate, so low.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The 1994 message built Forza Italia around a bloc against the left, so the distinction is central to it.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept, rejected by the movement's pro-enterprise stance.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The Lega ally said so, Berlusconi's own statements on Islam were mixed (including a 2001 remark on Western superiority not opened in sources); split.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The party was not confessional and based authority on elections.

social-market-economy.rationale: Wikipedia records that Forza Italia championed a social market economy and Berlusconi said a democracy cannot afford citizens in poor conditions.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Berlusconi's governments sent troops to Iraq and Afghanistan and were strongly Atlanticist.

rich-first.rationale: Liberismo and the entrepreneurial optimism of Berlusconism accept that wealth is created first by the successful.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Berlusconi moved Italy closer to the US and kept NATO ties, though he courted Putin, so neutrality is rejected.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist credit theory contradicts liberismo and a market banking sector.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: After 2011 Berlusconi attacked EU austerity and Merkel, but his own government passed an austerity package that year; split.

property-franchise.rationale: Berlusconism rests on mass electoral appeal and universal suffrage.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is not part of Berlusconism, which is pro-growth and conservative.

reification.rationale: A Marxist-Hegelian concept that the movement opposes; the question is theoretical.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Berlusconi himself owned national TV networks and newspapers, so adherents deny that wealthy ownership makes the press unfree.

racial-franchise.rationale: Berlusconi criticised the racial laws, and the movement operates in universal-suffrage democracy.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Contrary to a liberal-in-politics, non-confessional stance.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Berlusconi described himself as pro-Israel and condemned racial laws; targeted boycotts are rejected.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Internal religious matter; the party followed the Church while leaving moral questions to free votes.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Berlusconi, a billionaire, led a movement defending wealth creation; critics said his media concentration threatened liberty, but adherents reject the idea.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Berlusconi later accepted civil unions and the party had a liberal wing, though the topic was not salient.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Forza Italia called itself a Catholic party, though not confessional, so promoting atheism is the opposite.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The 1994 message pledged to combat crime, corruption and drugs, so abolition is rejected.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Liberista wing favours private charity but the party championed a social market economy with state protection; split.

term-limits.rationale: Berlusconi remained leader for decades and promoted strong premiership; adherents accept long tenure.

rent-control.rationale: Price controls contradict the liberista stance, and property owners were part of the base.

abolish-ip.rationale: Berlusconi owned a vast media company dependent on copyright; abolition would be against its interests.

uniformed-youth.rationale: A fascist institution; Berlusconi criticised parts of Mussolini's regime and the movement is liberal-democratic.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Berlusconi's Atlanticism accepted US bases in Italy.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Defending profit and ownership against the left, adherents reject discounting capital income.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Absolute pacifism is far from a movement that backed wars and law-and-order policy.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Berlusconi spoke in messianic terms about himself, but the movement framed politics as liberal enterprise against the left, not as spiritual war.

culture-before-state.rationale: The launch message put political action and reform first; a cultural-renewal-first line is not its approach.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Free-market liberismo rejects reserving the economy for a majority group.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A debate within the socialist movement; Berlusconism rejects socialism, so neither side matters.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public water and hospitals were not clear issues; social market wing accepts public provision, liberista wing wants privatisation.

second-chamber.rationale: Berlusconi proposed abolishing the Senate in favour of a leaner parliament, yet the 2006 reform kept a federal senate; split. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

municipal-property.rationale: Communalist ownership contradicts the movement's defence of private property.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Libertarian municipalism is far from a leader-centred party.

person-over-state.rationale: The Catholic-liberal self-description and the minimal friendly state serving citizens fit this statement.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Federalists in the party prefer entrenched regional powers while national-unity members accept revocability; split.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Not part of Berlusconism, which is civic and criticised racial laws.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Berlusconi's governments backed the Iraq invasion, which was not purely defensive.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Not a Berlusconian principle; he supported the Italian state as it stands.

communal-electorates.rationale: Contrary to a liberal-democratic, universal-suffrage framework.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not a Berlusconist theme; his enemy narrative targeted the left and prosecutors.

future-generations.rationale: A widely shared mainstream view that does not conflict with Berlusconism.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The sources record no claim about women's distinct values in politics, so adherents are neutral.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Berlusconi conducted personal diplomacy with Putin and Gaddafi; he favoured it closed and personal.

capital-controls.rationale: Liberismo opposes controls over movement of capital.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Berlusconi sent troops to Iraq and Afghanistan and the movement supports the armed forces.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Berlusconi promised tax cuts and later fought EU austerity rules but the party backed euro-era budget rules; split.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Revolutionary Marxist aim contradicts the movement.

sacred-nation.rationale: The launch message is patriotic but not mystical; mixed Alleanza Nazionale allies make it neutral.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Northern members believed the North subsidised the South, the opposite theory; Forza Italia's southern wing rejected both.

public-service-media.rationale: Berlusconi, as owner of Mediaset and while premier controlling state broadcaster RAI appointments, was criticised for undermining independent public media.

voter-id.rationale: Italy already requires ID at the polls and the movement never raised voter ID.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Berlusconi stressed election by the people as the source of legitimacy and a strong premiership, treating electoral victory as the mandate.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Berlusconism is Catholic-friendly but not confessional, with free votes on moral questions (s2); a literalist doctrine is not part of it.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Strong anti-communism is a core pillar of Berlusconism (s2, s3).

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Berlusconi governed with the Lega Nord, which wanted autonomy, but Forza Italia was not itself committed; adherents split.

simple-living.rationale: Berlusconism is a consumerist, business-led liberista politics (s1, s2), opposed to austerity of lifestyle.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Berlusconi was patriotic but the sources show no spiritual bond with the land as a theme.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The liberista programme favoured private property and free enterprise rather than common ownership of resources.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The populist appeal of a businessman against the old political class and a strong premiership sought direct contact with voters.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The programme's liberal rhetoric opposes state favouritism, though critics note conflicts of interest; this is the stated position.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Catholic-friendly but not confessional, with free votes on moral questions, so religion was not a basis of organisation.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Strong anti-communism and liberista economics reject Marxist labour value theory; Berlusconi's 1994 message frames communism as the enemy.

material-over-identity.rationale: Not a left movement, so the question has no direct application; Berlusconism was indifferent to the left's internal debate, so neutral.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Berlusconism is defined by strong anti-communism, so a communist-led socialist system is rejected outright; the 1994 message attacks the left as the threat.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Liberal wing wanted a minimal state but the party also championed a social market economy and promised higher minimum pensions, so adherents are split. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: The judiciary should not be able to obstruct the policies of a democratically elected government.
missingStatements.rationale: Berlusconi claimed persecution by prosecutors in 34 trials and compared himself to Enzo Tortora, pursuing judicial reform and ad personam laws.

missingStatements.text: Magistrates who investigate and prosecute should have separate careers from those who judge.
missingStatements.rationale: The Wikipedia article records that Berlusconi proposed separating magistrates' careers as part of reforming the judiciary.
missingStatements.declined: Italy-specific institutional detail on separating magistrates' careers; too narrow for the bank.

notes: Berlusconism was personalised and pragmatic: positions shifted over time (pro-EU in the 1990s, Eurosceptic after 2011) and the coalition mixed liberal, Christian-democratic, federalist and post-fascist wings. Confidence is mostly medium or low for social and foreign-policy items for that reason.
